summary: We made an interactive story map where NASA’s retired and abandoned hardware tells its own story to school-age space fans. Each stop on the Moon, Mars, deep space and Earth orbit is a “postcard” written in the spacecraft’s own voice. Kids learn what it was built to do, what science it made possible, and how its mission ended, with status badges for silent, retired, or still working. It shows that “abandoned” hardware, like the Apollo laser mirrors and the Voyagers, can still be doing science.
details: Postcards from the Left-Behind is a free, kid-friendly website for ages 8 to 14. A story map runs from Earth to the Moon, Mars, and deep space, with seven stops: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, the Apollo laser retroreflectors, the Opportunity rover, the Ingenuity helicopter, Pioneer 10 and 11, Voyager 1 and 2, and the Chandra X-ray Observatory. Tapping a stop opens a postcard with four parts: “Hello, I’m…”, “What I was built to do”, “The science I made possible”, and “How my story went.” Color-coded badges show each mission’s status. The Chandra stop includes NASA images and a 3D model that can be rotated. A 5-question quiz awards a Space Explorer badge, and a teacher page has discussion questions. We also made a short narrated animation and a presentation. The website is plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.We hope it helps students see that space hardware keeps teaching us after its mission ends.
dataRefs: We used NASA mission information and public NASA resources: facts about the Apollo rovers and retroreflectors, the Opportunity rover, the Ingenuity helicopter, Pioneer, Voyager, and the Chandra X-ray Observatory, plus NASA images and a NASA 3D model of Chandra from NASA websites.
